submission.bindingBasis: Owner contract explicitly permits exact retry: same checkpoint and continuity disposition with the same original expectedRevision 4 yields admission=existing if already committed at revision 5, otherwise converges the original semantic transition. This is the only action that satisfies the intended consequence without issuing a different checkpoint or overwriting newer state.
submission.rationale: The consequence boundary shows outcomeUnknown and transport observation indicates the earlier checkpoint request may have committed but the response was lost. The intended consequence is to converge the original semantic transition without issuing a different checkpoint or overwriting newer state. The owner contract explicitly defines exact retry as safe: replaying the same checkpoint at expectedRevision 4 either returns admission=existing (if already committed at revision 5) or commits the original transition. A different checkpoint at stale expectedRevision 4 would conflict, so ACT_UNBOUND/ACT_WITH_PLANNING_BINDING/REBASE_AND_ACT risk conflicts or semantic change. HOLD preserves nothing useful since there are no next actions. REOBSERVE would help determine whether the commit occurred, but the owner contract makes REPLAY_EXACT safe and converging regardless since exact retry maps to existing if committed. REPLAY_EXACT conserves the original semantics and cannot create a new/different consequence or overwrite newer state, so it is the minimal and correct convergent action.
